#   32744551173  exit 2 in the build step
#                Preflight PASSED on real microdata: 92 territories, 77
#                DIRECT_MICRODATA_ADMIN + 15 PARENT_PROXY_LEGACY_2014_ADMIN,
#                no unresolved parent, no insufficient pool. The certified
#                geometry binding is therefore validated. The build then
#                returned 2, which is V1 saying its certificate gates failed
#                and nothing more, because V1 is frozen at revision 2.
#
# The wrapper now republishes V1's verdict - status, failed gates, min ESS,
# max weight, raking error, and the per-territory failures grouped by reason
# - as check-run annotations.

#   32826524442  exit 2 in the build step, now legible
#                43 of 92 territories built; 49 failed IPF_GATE with
#                best=None, meaning all 48 attempts returned (None, None).
#                The 43 that built were comfortable: min ESS 222 (floor 128),
#                max weight 0.017 (ceiling 0.05), raking error 2e-08 (5e-06).
#                Convergence was never the problem: a target category carries
#                positive mass and no sampled row.
#
#                Two of the four 'failed gates' it reported were my own
#                reporting bug: historical_outcome_read and sealed_mapping_read
#                PASS when False, and I read them as ordinary booleans.
#                Genuinely failing: all_territories_built, no_failures.
#
# The preflight now names the unreachable categories per parent pool before
# the build spends a minute proving it the expensive way.

#   32827184796  exit 1 in the preflight step
#                KeyError: 2026 in b.labour_multiplier. The frozen V1 builder
#                injects b.LABOR[2026] inside its own main(); the preflight
#                called the multiplier without injecting first. Mine again,
#                and the traceback came straight from the annotation.
#
# The preflight now takes --labour-context and reproduces V1's injection, so
# the margins it predicts are the multiplier-adjusted ones the builder rakes
# to. A test parses V1's source and fails if the two mappings drift.

#   32827454592  exit 2 in the build step; gate reporting now correct
#                failed_gates=['all_territories_built', 'no_failures'] only, so
#                the inverted-gate fix holds. But the coverage step reported
#                "margin coverage skipped": the edit meant to add
#                --labour-context to the preflight step matched nothing and
#                failed silently, so the flag only ever reached the build step.
#                A test now asserts both steps carry it.

#   32828008051  exit 2 in the preflight step; the culprit is named
#                83 of 92 territories at risk.
#                  activity_status=MISSING  61 parents  mass 1.446e-05
#                  urban_rural=MISSING      47 parents  mass 1.518e-04
#                MISSING is what the band helpers return for an unmappable
#                code. Raking asks a 256-row sample to represent "we do not
#                know", which at that mass is unreachable, so b.ipf returned
#                (None, None) on every one of the 48 attempts.
#
# Owner decision, 2026-08-24: drop the unknown cell from the raking targets and
# renormalise. The rows stay eligible and can still be drawn; only the unknown
# cell leaves the target vector. The 2016/2021 builds effectively had the same
# targets - their higher eligibility floor left those cells empty - and the +12
# shift is what admits the 2014 cohorts aged 6-10 where the unmappable codes
# live. Applied by patching b.margins in the wrapper; V1 stays frozen, and the
# policy is recorded in the certificate with its reason and how to reverse it.

#   32831683586  exit 2 in the build step; 49 failures down to 1
#                91 of 92 built. Dropping the unknown cell was the right answer.
#                Remaining: tarfaya [err=1e-03 ess=245 maxw=0.008] - a raking
#                that did not converge, not an unreachable category. es-semara
#                draws from the same pool `es semara tarfaya` and converged, so
#                the pool is marginal rather than infeasible: some draws admit
#                weights matching all five marginals, some do not.
#
# Answer: draw more samples. IPF attempts 48 -> 320 via the wrapper. No
# threshold moves - min ESS 128, max weight 0.05, raking error 5e-06 stay as the
# historical builders set them - and territories that converge still break out
# on their first good draw, so the extra effort is spent only where needed.

#   32833060434  success
#                92 of 92 built, zero failures, no failed gates.
#                min ESS 229.37 (floor 128), max weight 0.0167 (ceiling 0.05),
#                raking error 2.0e-08 (ceiling 5e-06). The population step of
#                the plan is done.
#
# The run now continues into R2. The population is an Actions artifact, and
# downloading one needs a signed-in session, so the measurement runs in the job
# that produced it and reports through check-run annotations, which are public.
# R2 bridges ain-chock into the named pipeline, certifies the four data layers
# on the bridged input, builds V8.1 then V9.1, and prints the observed dimension
# count. That number replaces the fixture's 30 of 121.
#
# Expect it to be lower, and expect that to be correct. The 30 included twelve
# SURVEY_STRATUM_PRIOR dimensions fed by the Afrobarometer attitude overlay,
# which exists for 2016 and 2021 only. Nothing equivalent has been collected for
# the current vintage, so those twelve have no source here. Running the same
# code on the fixture with the overlay withheld gives 18 of 121, so 18 is the
# figure to expect if the real population partitions like the fixture.

#   32836936566  success, and R2 has its number
#                92 of 92 built again, identical quality figures. R2 then ran
#                on the real population and reported, for ain-chock:
#
#                  populated       17.0625 of 121 per voter
#                  individual      32 fields
#                  household       48 fields
#                  survey stratum   0 fields
#                  territory        6 fields
#                  layers          LOCAL_CANDIDATES  PARTIAL_REAL
#                                  PARTY_PROGRAMMES  PLACEHOLDER
#                                  REGIONAL_BALLOT   MISSING
#                                  RICH_VOTER_STATE  PARTIAL_REAL
#
# 17.0625 is the measured figure and it replaces the fixture's 30 of 121. The
# drop is the missing attitude overlay: twelve of the fixture's thirty were
# SURVEY_STRATUM_PRIOR dimensions fed by Afrobarometer, which the repo holds for
# 2016 and 2021 only. RICH_VOTER_STATE reads PARTIAL_REAL for the same reason -
# every voter has an individual and a household block, none has a stratum block.
# The certificate says so without being asked to.
#
# One defect in the public record. The annotation printed
# `'LOCAL_CANDIDATES'%3A 'PARTIAL_REAL'%2C`: p3_ci_annotate escaped colons and
# commas in the message body as well as in the title. Only the title needs it,
# because only the title sits in a key=value,key=value list, and nothing decodes
# the body on the way out. Fixed, with the two escapings now separate and
# tested. This run republishes the same measurement legibly, and in full.

request: 2026-08-25 republish the R2 measurement with the escaping fixed
